title: Cross-Harness AGENTS.md and Instruction Architecture Remediation
pipeline_rationale: The work changes global instructions, skills, and configuration and includes one authentication-bearing OpenCode JSONC property. Classification is uncertain because a security-sensitive shared-runtime field is touched; the standard path retains independent review, explicit backups, deterministic validation, and fresh-process checks instead of the abbreviated bookkeeping path.
skipped_stages: Stage 4: skipped because no production-code behavior is being authored.
Stage 4b: skipped because no RED test authoring applies to instruction/configuration files.
Stage 6: skipped because deterministic structural/configuration checks replace an application test suite.
Stage 8: skipped because validation is deterministic and no correction-cycle trigger is present at plan creation.
summary: Remediate AGENTS.md architecture, progressive disclosure, shared Codex/OpenCode rule storage, agent-writer standards, project instruction files, and environment-variable references.
keyOutcomes: Canonical shared rule modules under the OpenCode user folder
Current agent templates and deterministic validation
Commented user-level OpenCode environment source of truth preserved
risks: Over-aggressive extraction could remove a safety rule from always-on context
Global configuration edits could affect new sessions
Existing unrelated dirty-worktree changes could be overwritten if edits are broad
dependencies: Fresh-session validation after global instruction changes
validationCriteria: No active agent template uses deprecated tools frontmatter
OpenCode config contains no affected inline credential value
